title: authz oracle misreports three authenticated routes as open: it does not resolve the `_require_auth_api` alias
class: self-reporting control: the gate oracle reads decorator NAMES, not the decorators that run
evidence: /api/s3-generation-jobs/<id>, /api/s4-execution-jobs/<id>, /api/s3-generation-jobs/<id>/cancel listed as '(none — auth/login only or open)'; views.py:245 `from primeqa.core.auth import require_auth as _require_auth_api`; the three routes carry @_require_auth_api
expected: the oracle names the gate that actually runs on every route
observed: any alias of a gate is invisible to it; the oracle can be green while a route is open, or red while it is gated — its report is not evidence of either
proposed_fix: derive gates from the live app (walk __wrapped__ / closure args) or resolve import aliases in the AST; add a guard asserting the oracle and the live map agree

title: the template dead-link sweep silently excludes every href that carries a Jinja expression
class: a sweep that skips what it cannot parse reports the residue as clean
reproduction: sed -n 63p tests/unit/test_step_6a_routes.py — href regex is /[^"{}\s]*/, so any href containing `{` is never checked; scripts/audit/deadlinks.py url_map.json finds what it skipped
evidence: 166 internal targets in templates+JS; the unit sweep can see at most the 60 with no Jinja; 5 dead targets found, 2 on live pages (AUD-003, AUD-004); the sweep also ignores action=, hx-*, data-confirm-form and fetch() literals
expected: a dead-link sweep resolves every target a browser or htmx will follow, parameterised or not
observed: the sweep has been green through D-490, D-491 and the retirement while two dead links sat on live pages
proposed_fix: replace the sweep's regex with scripts/audit/deadlinks.py's resolver (all attributes, Jinja collapsed to a wildcard segment, if-branches expanded) and gate on zero dead

title: six templates are rendered by nothing; one of them is documented in CLAUDE.md as a live component and its JS calls a retired v1 API
class: documentation asserts a component the code no longer wires
surface: primeqa/templates: claims/inbox.html, claims/list.html, components/_legacy_banner.html, components/feedback_modal.html, dashboard_release.html, run/index.html; static/js/tc_feedback.js
reproduction: diff <(find primeqa/templates -name '*.html' | sed 's|primeqa/templates/||' | sort) <(grep -rhoE "render_template\(\s*['\"][^'\"]+|\{%\s*(include|extends|import|from)\s+['\"][^'\"]+" primeqa/ | grep -oE "[a-z_/.]+\.html" | sort -u)
evidence: zero render_template/include/extends references to the six; no dynamic render_template calls exist; CLAUDE.md 'UI component kit' lists `feedback_modal.html` + `static/js/tc_feedback.js` as the thumbs-feedback component; tc_feedback.js:31 calls /api/test-cases/${tcId}/feedback, a route absent from url_map
expected: CLAUDE.md describes components that exist in the running product
observed: a documented component is dead code calling a dead endpoint
proposed_fix: delete the six templates and tc_feedback.js; correct the CLAUDE.md component kit list

title: the public shared-dashboard link and its mint endpoint 500 on every call: `_hash_share_token` was deleted in the v1 retirement while both callers stayed
class: retirement removed a symbol whose callers survived (same cause as the plan_id-never-selected and dead-link findings)
reproduction: GET /shared/anything → 500; grep -rn 'def _hash_share_token' primeqa/ → 0 definitions; git log -S 'def _hash_share_token' → removed in 7fd518f (D-221.4)
evidence: render sweep: /shared/no-such-token → NameError: name '_hash_share_token' is not defined, for every session; the route is unauthenticated by design (the token is the capability), so every share link ever issued now 500s, and no new one can be minted
expected: a bad token renders the not_found state (404); a good token renders the read-only dashboard; the mint returns a URL
observed: NameError → the themed 500 page, on both routes, since the retirement commit
proposed_fix: either restore a hashing helper (sha256, as the poll-token one) or retire both routes and the shared_dashboard_links table with them; add a guard that every name referenced in views.py resolves (pyflakes F821 as a gate test)

title: landing page 500s for a tenant with no runs: the template compares a None pass rate to an integer
class: a data shape nobody planned: the zero-state of an aggregate
reproduction: log in as a member of a tenant with zero execution runs (scratch tenant 2); GET /
evidence: render sweep, member_t2: GET / → TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int' at dashboard.html:50; the stats builder yields pass_rate=None when there are no runs
expected: a tenant with no runs sees a landing page with an empty pass-rate cell
observed: the themed 500 page; a brand-new tenant's first screen is an error
proposed_fix: coerce pass_rate to 0 (or render an empty state) in the stats builder, and render the legacy dashboard over a zero-run fixture in a page test

title: requirement page: the readiness handler commented 'never breaks the page' raises NameError itself — `logging` is not imported in views.py
class: self-reporting control: a safety net whose own body cannot run (the fifth instance)
surface: GET /requirements/<id> — views.py:2982-2983 (`except Exception: logging.getLogger(...)`), inside requirements_detail
reproduction: pyflakes primeqa/views.py → 'views.py:2983 undefined name logging'; grep -c '^import logging' primeqa/views.py → 0; make readiness_for_pairs raise (substrate unreachable, a claim with no coverage rows in an odd shape) and GET the requirement page
evidence: the try/except at views.py:2970-2984 exists so that a readiness failure degrades to an empty readiness map; its except clause calls logging.getLogger, and `logging` is undefined in the module, so the handler raises NameError and the page returns the themed 500 — exactly when the net was meant to hold
expected: a readiness read failure logs a warning and the requirement page renders without readiness cells
observed: a readiness read failure becomes a 500; every day the handler is not exercised it reads as working — this is a control that reports its own correctness in a comment
proposed_fix: import logging at module level (views.py uses `log`/`logger` elsewhere — use the module logger); add pyflakes F821 as a gate test so an undefined name in a handler cannot ship; add a page test that forces readiness_for_pairs to raise and asserts 200

title: Jira ticket search 500s whenever an environment or connection is chosen: `_jira_client` / `_jira_client_for_env` are undefined
class: retirement removed a symbol whose callers survived (same cause as the plan_id-never-selected and dead-link findings)
surface: GET /api/jira/search — primeqa/execution/routes.py:65,70 (the survivor of the v1 execution module; execution_bp is registered at app.py:69)
reproduction: as any member: GET /api/jira/search?q=abc&environment_id=4 → 500 {SERVER_ERROR}; log: NameError: name '_jira_client' is not defined. Without an env/conn the route short-circuits to a hint and the defect hides
evidence: pyflakes: execution/routes.py:65 undefined name '_jira_client', :70 '_jira_client_for_env'; the render sweep's plain GET returned 200 with the 'pick an environment' hint, which is why a 200-only sweep would never see it
expected: a Jira search against a configured connection returns matching tickets for the requirement picker
observed: any real search dies before reaching Jira; the picker that depends on it cannot work
proposed_fix: restore the two helpers (they lived in the retired v1 metadata/jira module) on the runs Jira client, or retire the route and the picker together; the F821 gate closes the class

title: release create/update/add-requirement 500 on oversize or wrong-type input: the database is the only validator
class: no validation at the boundary — the database column is the validator and it answers 500
reproduction: as a member: POST /api/releases {"name": "A"*20000} → 500; PATCH /api/releases/58 {"name": "A"*20000} → 500; POST /api/releases/58/requirements {"requirement_id": "x"} → 500; the HTML /releases form with a 20k name → the themed 500 page
evidence: scripts/audit/post_all.py on scratch: 4 of 650 hostile POSTs 500; psycopg2 StringDataRightTruncation 'value too long for type character varying(255)' ×3 and InvalidTextRepresentation 'invalid input syntax for type integer: "x"' ×1; stacks end in release/repository.py:27 and :80 and release/service.py:125 with no length or type check on the way
expected: 400 with a message naming the field; nothing reaches the database
observed: an unhandled DataError; the server log carries a stack for every oversize submission; the user sees 'Something went wrong'
proposed_fix: validate name/description length and integer ids in ReleaseService (create_section already does this for sections — copy that shape); a boundary test that POSTs 20k-char and wrong-type bodies to every create/update route and asserts 4xx

title: any member can mint, rotate or revoke ANY release's public status-poll token; CLAUDE.md says Release-Owner or admin
class: documentation claims a gate the route does not enforce (self-reporting control)
surface: POST and DELETE /api/releases/<id>/status-token — release/routes.py:341-378, gated @require_role('admin','tester') = MEMBER floor, no owner check in the body
reproduction: as scratch member user 14 (not the creator of release 58): POST /api/releases/58/status-token → 201 with a fresh token; POST again → 201 (rotated: the previous token, held by CI, is now dead); DELETE → 200 revoked
evidence: post_all.py: four 201s and four 200s for member_t1 on these routes; the body reads only get_release(release_id, tenant_id) then writes status_poll_token_hash; CLAUDE.md 'Public release-status endpoint is token-gated … Mint + revoke are Release-Owner/admin, tenant-scoped'
expected: only the release owner or an admin can expose a release's decision status to an unauthenticated poller, or invalidate the token CI already holds
observed: every member of the tenant can do both, for every release; the act is logged but not gated
proposed_fix: gate at Tier.ADMIN or add the owner check (release.created_by == request.user['id']); correct CLAUDE.md or the code so they agree; add the route to the authz inventory's expected-tier table

title: PASS 4: an execution can be enqueued with NO plan — the 'every run starts from a RECORDED plan' invariant (D-486) is not enforced at the enqueue chokepoint
class: an invariant enforced at some entry points and asserted for all of them (self-reporting control)
surface: POST /api/s4-execution-jobs (views.py:4535 → execution_engine/intake.py:enqueue_s4_execution, plan_id Optional=None); the same intake serves POST /claims/<id>/run and /claims/<id>/run-async
reproduction: on scratch, as an admin (tenant 1): plant an approved claim with an active metadata recipe; POST /api/s4-execution-jobs {test_id, environment_id: 4} with no plan → 202 {job_id: 131, status: queued}; SELECT plan_id FROM s4_execution_jobs WHERE id=131 → NULL. Two earlier attempts were refused for OTHER reasons (environment scope; no executable recipe) — none of the refusals was 'no plan'
evidence: job 131 queued on scratch with plan_id NULL, created_by 15; intake.enqueue_s4_execution signature `plan_id: Optional[str] = None`; the route's own docstring names a production-confirm gate and an admin gate and no plan gate; D-486 records 'every execution starts from a RECORDED plan … /run retired', and the memory ledger already counts 568 plan-less stamped runs since the re-enable as evidence
expected: a loud refusal naming the missing plan, at the ONE execution chokepoint, for every entry point
observed: the release, requirement and schedule entry points plan first; the API and the two claim-level routes hand the intake a job with no plan and it accepts it — the invariant holds by convention of the caller, not by the chokepoint
proposed_fix: make plan_id REQUIRED in enqueue_s4_execution and refuse without it (PlanRefused), then either point the claim-level routes and the API at the planner (plan-for-one-claim) or retire them as /run was; add a guard test that enqueues without a plan through every route and asserts the refusal. The 568 plan-less runs already on production are the evidence this path is exercised
